title: Stability of Low-Rank Implicit Regularization in Perturbed Deep Matrix Factorization
summary: This paper studies the stability of low-rank implicit regularization in deep matrix factorization, a tractable model for understanding how gradient-based training can favor low-complexity structure. We first revisit the noiseless setting and derive sufficient spectral conditions under which gradient descent exhibits a nonempty low-rank interval. These conditions clarify how the target spectrum, initialization, and step size jointly determine when a low-rank phase is observable along the optimization trajectory.
